title: Replace Elements in an Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed array of n distinct positive integers, perform m operations where each operation replaces an element in the array with a new value.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array of n distinct positive integers, perform m operations where each operation replaces an element in the array with a new value. Ensure the new value is not already in the array. Return the array after all operations.
constraints: Each operation [old,new] replaces the currently present old value, and new is not currently present.
Return the final array in its original positional order.
hints: A value-to-index map locates every currently present value in constant expected time.
For each operation, remove old from the map, write new at that index, and map new to the same index.
Maintain both the result list and positions dictionary through all operations.
The invariant maps every current array value to its unique position, making each sequential replacement exact.
editorial: The invariant maps every current array value to its unique position, making each sequential replacement exact.

tests.explanation: The replacements update positions to produce [3,2,7,1].
Both operations affect the same position in sequence, producing [4,2].
